THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: Consumer surplus is the difference between a buyer's willingness to pay and the price actually paid. Surplus analysis compares value created with the opportunity cost of the resources used. Demand can be interpreted as buyers' marginal willingness to pay. The gain from an additional trade is the buyer’s willingness to pay minus the seller’s cost, not either side’s individual surplus alone.

WORKED EXAMPLE: CALCULATING CONSUMER SURPLUS

runs.text: Price ($) is vertical; Quantity is horizontal. Demand intercepts price at $30. Supply and demand meet at quantity 8, price $14. Consumer surplus is the triangle below demand and above $14 up to quantity 8, with area $64.

runs.text: 1 divided by 2 times 8 times open parenthesis 30 dollars minus 14 dollars close parenthesis equals 64 dollars

transcript.sourceText: At equilibrium, price is $14 and quantity is 8. The demand intercept of $30 represents the highest willingness to pay. Consumer surplus is the triangle above price and below demand: 1/2 x 8 x ($30 - $14) = $64.
